title: A 1996 Illinois questionnaire backs same-sex marriage and a handgun ban
tease: Running for the Illinois Senate, Obama’s IVI survey supports legalizing same-sex marriage and banning handguns.
summary: During the 1996 Illinois Senate race, Obama’s Independent Voters of Illinois questionnaire supports legalizing same-sex marriage and a ban on the manufacture, sale, and possession of handguns. He later says the handgun answer is not his writing. The marriage line is the high-water mark of his early LGBTQ stance before he moves to civil unions.

links.label: Social policy of the Obama administration

title: Chicago speech calls Iraq a dumb war
tease: At Federal Plaza, state senator Obama opposes invading Iraq without a case that meets a just-war test.
summary: On October 2, 2002, state senator Obama tells an anti-war rally at Chicago’s Federal Plaza that he is not opposed to all wars, only dumb ones. He argues there is no imminent threat from Saddam Hussein and that an invasion would inflame the Middle East. The speech becomes the core of his 2008 foreign-policy contrast with Hillary Clinton and John McCain.

title: 2003 Illinois death-row reforms, with capital punishment kept for the worst crimes
tease: Obama helps make Illinois videotape homicide interrogations and wants a shorter list of death-eligible killings.
summary: As an Illinois senator Obama helps pass the first statewide mandate to videotape homicide interrogations and pushes to shrink the “laundry list” of aggravating factors that make a killing death-eligible. He still supports capital punishment for crimes so heinous — mass murder, the rape and murder of a child — that “the community is justified in expressing the full measure of its outrage,” even while saying the penalty deters little. No federal prisoner is executed during his presidency.

links.label: Social policy of the Obama administration
Illinois Senate career of Barack Obama

title: U.S. Senate run backs civil unions, not marriage
tease: The 2004 Senate campaign supports equal legal rights for gay couples while keeping marriage as a word for the states.
summary: Running for the U.S. Senate in 2004, Obama supports civil unions that confer equal state rights on same-sex couples and opposes a federal marriage amendment. He does not support using the word marriage. That formula — rights without the name — holds through the 2008 presidential campaign.

links.label: Social policy of the Obama administration

title: Senate vote to ease Bush stem-cell limits
tease: Obama backs the Stem Cell Research Enhancement Act, later vetoed, and condemns the White House for blocking it.
summary: Obama votes for the 2006 Stem Cell Research Enhancement Act, which would loosen President Bush’s limits on embryonic stem-cell lines. Bush vetoes the bill. Obama says Democrats, some conservative Republicans, and the public want the research, and that only the White House is standing in the way of potential cures.

links.label: Social policy of the Obama administration

title: Chicago Council speech: end Iraq, grow the Army, talk to enemies
tease: Obama’s first major foreign-policy address pairs a responsible Iraq exit with more troops and diplomacy.
summary: At the Chicago Council on Global Affairs, Obama sets five foreign-policy tests: a responsible end to the Iraq War, a larger Army and Marine Corps, securing nuclear material, rebuilding alliances (including on climate), and more foreign aid. He is already willing to talk to adversaries without Bush-era preconditions — the seed of later Cuba and Iran diplomacy.

links.label: Foreign policy of the Obama administration

title: Primary fight: no individual mandate
tease: Obama’s 2008 plan has subsidies and a public option, and treats Clinton’s buy-insurance rule as coercion.
summary: In the 2008 Democratic primary Obama’s health plan offers subsidies, an employer requirement, and a public option, but no individual mandate. He argues people lack insurance because they cannot afford it, not because they refuse to buy it, and that forcing a purchase is the wrong lever. A year later the mandate is in his bill.

title: Campaign says DEA will stop raiding state-legal dispensaries
tease: A spokesman tells the San Francisco Chronicle that Obama would end raids on medical marijuana that follows state law.
summary: In May 2008 a campaign spokesman tells the San Francisco Chronicle that an Obama Justice Department would stop DEA raids on medical-marijuana suppliers operating under state law. Attorney General Eric Holder repeats a version of that line in 2009. By 2012, federal raids have exceeded the Bush administration’s pace.

links.label: Social policy of the Obama administration

title: Votes for the FISA Amendments Act
tease: After promising to fight warrantless wiretapping, Obama votes to legalize the telecom-assisted surveillance architecture.
summary: On July 9, 2008, Obama votes for the FISA Amendments Act, which becomes the statutory home of programs later disclosed as PRISM. Civil-liberties groups call it a flip from his earlier promise to filibuster telecom immunity and warrantless collection. As president he defends the system as narrow and necessary, then offers modest limits after Snowden.

title: A New Strategy for a New World
tease: The July 2008 address pairs ending Iraq with finishing the fight in Afghanistan and locking down nuclear material.
summary: In Washington, Obama lists five goals: end the Iraq War responsibly, finish the fight against al-Qaeda and the Taliban, secure nuclear weapons, achieve energy security, and rebuild alliances. Afghanistan is framed as the necessary war Iraq distracted from. Closing Guantanamo and changing detention policy sit in the same campaign packet.

title: Unsolicited 2008 disability platform
tease: Obama is the only Democratic presidential candidate to put out a full disability agenda, including the ADA restoration fight.
summary: Around the Americans with Disabilities Act anniversary in 2008, Obama issues a disability-policy statement covering the ADA Restoration Act and the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities. Wikipedia’s social-policy article notes he was the only Democratic candidate to do so unsolicited.

links.label: Social policy of the Obama administration

title: Third debate: Roe, and nobody’s pro-abortion
tease: Obama defends legal abortion under Roe, wants fewer unintended pregnancies, and rejects a late-term ban without health exceptions.
summary: In the third 2008 presidential debate Obama restates his Roe v. Wade support and says the country can still reduce unintended pregnancies through education, contraception, and adoption. As an Illinois senator he had opposed “born alive” bills he said would interfere with a woman’s right to choose, while also saying some late-term limits could be acceptable with physical and mental-health exceptions.

links.label: Social policy of the Obama administration

title: Executive order to close Guantanamo within a year
tease: Two days after taking office, Obama orders the prison shuttered. Congress later blocks transfers to the United States.
summary: Executive Order 13492 directs that the Guantanamo Bay detention camp close within a year and that detainees be reviewed case by case. Transfers cut the population sharply over two terms. Congress bans moving detainees onto U.S. soil, and 41 men are still held when Obama leaves office.

links.label: Foreign policy of the Obama administration

title: Signs the $800 billion Recovery Act
tease: ARRA mixes tax cuts, unemployment aid, infrastructure, and clean-energy money in the trough of the Great Recession.
summary: Obama signs the American Recovery and Reinvestment Act, an $800 billion (later scored near $831 billion) stimulus of spending and tax cuts. It extends unemployment insurance, funds infrastructure and education, and becomes the administration’s first large clean-energy investment. Job growth turns consistently positive by early 2011.

links.label: American Recovery and Reinvestment Act of 2009
Economic policy of the Obama administration

title: Executive order lifts Bush stem-cell limits
tease: Order 13505 allows federally funded embryonic stem-cell research within the law and revokes Bush’s 2007 restrictions.
summary: Obama signs Executive Order 13505, allowing responsible human embryonic stem-cell research to the extent permitted by law and revoking George W. Bush’s 2007 order. It completes the fight he waged as a senator when two enhancement bills died by veto.

links.label: Social policy of the Obama administration

title: GM files bankruptcy under the auto rescue
tease: The administration continues the Bush-era rescue and puts GM and Chrysler through structured bankruptcies.
summary: General Motors files for Chapter 11 on June 1, 2009, after Chrysler’s April filing. Obama’s auto task force uses TARP money to restructure both firms instead of letting them liquidate, with new labor terms and a government equity stake. The rescue is already underway under Bush; Obama owns the conditions.

title: Race to the Top invites states to compete for school grants
tease: A $4.35 billion ARRA pot pushes standards, data systems, and teacher evaluation instead of a single federal curriculum.
summary: The Education Department launches Race to the Top on July 24, 2009, using Recovery Act money as competitive grants. Obama treats it as the main federal lever on K–12: states adopt reforms to win funds rather than Washington writing a national curriculum.

title: Signs the Shepard-Byrd hate-crime law
tease: Federal hate-crime law now covers sexual orientation, gender identity, gender, and disability.
summary: Obama signs the Matthew Shepard and James Byrd Jr. Hate Crimes Prevention Act on October 28, 2009. It adds sexual orientation, gender identity, gender, and disability to the federal hate-crime statute. The bill had been a long-running Democratic LGBTQ and civil-rights ask; Obama had promised to sign it.

links.label: Matthew Shepard and James Byrd Jr. Hate Crimes Prevention Act
Social policy of the Obama administration

title: West Point speech sends 30,000 more troops to Afghanistan
tease: Obama announces a surge with a 2011 start to the drawdown, calling Afghanistan the war that has to be won.
summary: At West Point, Obama orders roughly 30,000 additional U.S. troops to Afghanistan and says a drawdown will begin in July 2011. He frames it as finishing the fight against al-Qaeda that Iraq postponed. The extra force is real; so is the later unwind that still leaves thousands in place through 2017.

links.label: Foreign policy of the Obama administration

title: Senate health bill passes without a public option
tease: The Senate’s Christmas Eve vote keeps the individual mandate and drops the government insurance plan Obama wanted.
summary: The Senate passes its health bill 60–39 on Christmas Eve without a public option, after Lieberman and others refuse to support one. The individual mandate, exchanges, and Medicaid expansion remain. Obama accepts the trade to keep the rest of the bill alive, while still describing a public plan as his preference.

title: Signs the Affordable Care Act
tease: The law adds exchanges, subsidies, a Medicaid expansion, and the mandate Obama ran against two years earlier.
summary: Obama signs the Affordable Care Act on March 23, 2010. Major coverage provisions take effect in 2014. By 2016 the law covers about 20–24 million more people and the uninsured rate has fallen from roughly 16% to 9%. No House Republicans, and only a few Senate Republicans, vote for it. The CBO scores it as a modest deficit reducer.

title: Deepwater drilling moratorium after the BP spill
tease: The administration pauses new deepwater wells in the Gulf, a break from the all-of-the-above leasing pitch.
summary: After the Deepwater Horizon blowout, Interior issues a deepwater drilling moratorium on May 27, 2010. Obama had spent the spring promoting an energy plan that included some offshore expansion. The pause is temporary; leasing later resumes under tighter rules, still inside an all-of-the-above frame that also funded renewables.

links.label: Energy policy of the Obama administration

title: Signs Dodd–Frank and creates the CFPB
tease: The 2010 bank law tightens risk rules and adds a consumer bureau, without breaking up the largest banks.
summary: Obama signs the Dodd–Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act, the main statutory answer to the 2008 crash. It creates the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau and the Financial Stability Oversight Council and tightens oversight of shadow banking. It does not restore Glass–Steagall or break up the banks that grew larger in the crisis.

links.label: Economic policy of the Obama administration

title: DREAM Act dies in the Senate
tease: A filibuster kills the bill that would have given a path to people brought to the U.S. as children. DACA is still 18 months away.
summary: On December 18, 2010, the DREAM Act fails a Senate cloture vote, 55–41. Obama had backed the bill as the legislative path for people brought to the country as children. The collapse is the backdrop for his 2011 claim that he could not defer deportations by himself, and for DACA in 2012.

title: Signs the Don’t Ask, Don’t Tell repeal
tease: The 2010 law ends the ban on openly gay, lesbian, and bisexual service members after a Pentagon review.
summary: Obama signs the Don’t Ask, Don’t Tell Repeal Act of 2010, ending the 1993 policy that barred openly gay service. Certification and implementation follow in 2011. It is the first major LGBTQ statute of the presidency, months before he still says he personally opposes same-sex marriage.

links.label: Don't Ask, Don't Tell Repeal Act of 2010

title: NATO-led intervention in Libya begins
tease: Obama helps organize air and naval strikes that, with European partners, end Gaddafi’s regime without a U.S. occupation.
summary: On March 19, 2011, a U.S.-supported coalition begins strikes in Libya under a UN civilian-protection mandate. Obama describes it as a case for using force with allies and without a large American ground force. The campaign contributes to the fall of Muammar Gaddafi later that year.

links.label: Foreign policy of the Obama administration

title: “I am not king”: no unilateral deferred action yet
tease: At a Univision forum Obama says he cannot change immigration law by himself, a year before he creates DACA.
summary: On March 28, 2011, Obama tells a Univision town hall that the idea he can change immigration law unilaterally is false: he is president, not king. He still backs the DREAM Act in Congress. Fourteen months later he announces Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals, using enforcement discretion he had said was not available.

title: Drawdown from the Afghan surge begins
tease: Obama announces that surge troops will start coming home, shifting Afghanistan from build-up to unwind.
summary: In a June 22, 2011, address Obama says 10,000 troops will leave Afghanistan by the end of the year and that the surge force will be gone by summer 2012. The war is not over. By the end of his presidency about 8,400 U.S. soldiers remain, far below the peak and far from zero.

links.label: Foreign policy of the Obama administration

title: Drone strike kills Anwar al-Awlaki in Yemen
tease: A U.S. citizen is killed in a CIA drone strike, the sharpest example of Obama’s expanded targeted-killing program.
summary: A CIA drone strike in Yemen kills Anwar al-Awlaki, a U.S.-born al-Qaeda in the Arabian Peninsula propagandist, on September 30, 2011. The administration defends the strike as lawful against an imminent operational threat. Critics call it an extrajudicial killing of a citizen. Armed drones are by then a signature Obama tool in Pakistan, Yemen, and Somalia.

links.label: Foreign policy of the Obama administration

title: U.S. combat forces leave Iraq
tease: The 2011 withdrawal completes the 2002 speech and the 2008 pledge, before later strikes against ISIS.
summary: The last U.S. combat brigade leaves Iraq in December 2011, ending the war Obama opposed from Chicago and ran against in 2008. A small residual presence and, after 2014, a campaign against ISIS sit outside that original war. On the invasion itself, the public record never flips.

links.label: Withdrawal of United States troops from Iraq (2011)
Foreign policy of the Obama administration

title: Federal raid on Oaksterdam University
tease: A high-profile DEA action in Oakland shows the 2008 no-raid pledge has not held for state-legal cannabis.
summary: On April 2, 2012, federal agents raid Oaksterdam University, Richard Lee’s Oakland medical-marijuana training site. By then the Obama administration has surpassed Bush-era raid counts. Legislators from five states ask the Justice Department to stop targeting shops that follow state law. The Cole memo is still a year away.

links.label: Social policy of the Obama administration

title: Tells ABC he supports same-sex marriage
tease: In a Robin Roberts interview Obama becomes the first sitting president to back legalizing same-sex marriage.
summary: On May 9, 2012, Obama tells ABC’s Robin Roberts that same-sex couples should be able to marry. He cites staff, troops, and his own family, and says his view has evolved. He had opposed using the word marriage as recently as 2010, while supporting civil unions and, later, a DOMA repeal. The Justice Department had already stopped defending DOMA in 2011.

links.label: BBC: Obama says same-sex couples should be able to marry
Social policy of the Obama administration

title: DACA offers deferred action to Dreamers
tease: After Congress fails on the DREAM Act, DHS creates a two-year, renewable deferral for people brought to the U.S. as children.
summary: On June 15, 2012, the administration announces Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals. Qualifying people who arrived as children can receive a renewable two-year deferral from deportation and a work permit. It is the policy Obama said in 2011 he lacked power to create by himself. By the 2020s hundreds of thousands of people hold DACA status.

title: Chemical-weapons red line in Syria
tease: Obama says moving or using chemical weapons would change his calculus, a line read as a strike threat.
summary: At an August 20, 2012, press conference Obama says the use or movement of chemical weapons in Syria would be a red line that changed his calculus. Supporters hear a commitment to strike. A year later, after the Ghouta attack, he asks Congress for authorization and then accepts a Russia-brokered deal to remove the stockpile instead.

links.label: Foreign policy of the Obama administration

title: Signs the American Taxpayer Relief Act
tease: The deal lets Bush-era tax cuts expire for high earners and keeps them for everyone else.
summary: Obama signs the American Taxpayer Relief Act on January 2, 2013. The Bush tax cuts expire at the top, a sequester caps some spending, and the deficit later falls back toward its historical share of GDP. Against a baseline where all the cuts expired, the law still added to future deficits.

links.label: Economic policy of the Obama administration

title: Post–Sandy Hook gun package, including an assault-weapons ban
tease: After the Newtown shooting Obama asks Congress for a new assault-weapons ban, magazine limits, and background checks.
summary: On January 16, 2013, a month after Sandy Hook, Obama announces 23 executive actions and asks Congress to renew an assault-weapons ban, limit magazines, and expand background checks. Universal checks fail in the Senate that April. The proposals match a long-standing Senate record in favor of the 1994 ban’s reauthorization and against liability shields for gun makers.

links.label: Social policy of the Obama administration

title: Second inaugural names gay rights
tease: Obama is the first president to use the word gay in an inaugural address, tying Stonewall to Seneca Falls and Selma.
summary: In his second inaugural address Obama says the journey is not complete until gay brothers and sisters are treated like anyone else under the law. It is the first time a president has said “gay” in an inaugural. He had already announced support for same-sex marriage; this puts it in the civic canon beside voting rights and women’s rights.

title: State of the Union asks for a $9 federal minimum wage
tease: Inequality is “the defining challenge of our time.” The wage floor request later rises to $10.10, then $12.
summary: In the 2013 State of the Union Obama asks Congress to raise the federal minimum wage to $9 and index it. He later moves the ask to $10.10. The Republican Congress never passes it. Several states raise their own floors, which the administration treats as partial success on pre-tax inequality after tax increases on high earners in the American Taxpayer Relief Act.

links.label: Economic policy of the Obama administration

title: Cole memo stands down federal marijuana cases in regulated states
tease: James Cole tells prosecutors not to spend resources on regulated state marijuana that meets federal priorities.
summary: The Cole Memorandum, issued August 29, 2013, tells U.S. attorneys that limited Justice Department resources should not target marijuana activity that is legal under a tightly regulated state system, except where federal priorities (cartels, violence, kids, interstate trafficking) are at stake. It is the delayed fulfillment of the 2008 raid pledge, after the 2010–2012 enforcement spike.

title: Asks Congress before a Syria strike, then takes the Russia deal
tease: After Ghouta, Obama steps back from an imminent strike and pursues a diplomatic destruction of Syria’s declared chemical weapons.
summary: On August 31, 2013, Obama announces he will seek congressional authorization for a limited Syria strike rather than act immediately. The administration then accepts a Russian proposal to account for and destroy Syria’s declared chemical arsenal. The red-line threat is not carried out as a bombing campaign.

links.label: Foreign policy of the Obama administration

title: Post-Snowden speech defends NSA collection with new limits
tease: Obama calls the programs circumscribed and necessary, and promises court review for bulk telephone metadata.
summary: On January 17, 2014, Obama defends NSA collection as a narrow system to protect the country and announces new limits, including court approval for some telephone-record queries and a plan to move bulk metadata out of government hands. Privacy groups call the speech vague. The USA Freedom Act in 2015 later ends the NSA’s own bulk phone-record stockpile.

title: Sanctions after Russia annexes Crimea
tease: Obama and European partners start a sanctions campaign that later feeds a Russian financial squeeze.
summary: On March 17, 2014, the United States announces sanctions on Russian officials after the Crimea annexation. Obama treats it as a case for coordinated economic pressure rather than military pushback in Ukraine. Later rounds, with the EU, contribute to a Russian financial crisis.

links.label: International sanctions during the Russo-Ukrainian War
Foreign policy of the Obama administration

title: Announces restored diplomatic relations with Cuba
tease: After Vatican and Canadian mediation, Obama and Raúl Castro agree to reopen embassies and ease parts of the embargo.
summary: On December 17, 2014, Obama and Cuban leader Raúl Castro announce a normalization deal: prisoners swapped, diplomatic ties restored, and some travel and trade rules eased. The statutory embargo remains; the policy of isolation does not. Obama had kept the embargo while loosening family remittances in 2009. This is the break.

links.label: Foreign policy of the Obama administration

title: Signs the USA Freedom Act
tease: The 2015 law ends NSA bulk storage of domestic telephone metadata and leaves Section 702 collection in place.
summary: Obama signs the USA Freedom Act on June 2, 2015. Telephone metadata stays with the carriers; the government needs a court order to query it. Section 702 overseas collection — the legal basis for PRISM — continues. The vote is a partial answer to Snowden and to Obama’s own 2008 FISA vote, not a reversal of the surveillance state.

title: Obergefell makes same-sex marriage the law
tease: The Supreme Court legalizes same-sex marriage nationwide. Obama had already said the Equal Protection Clause requires it.
summary: Obergefell v. Hodges holds that the Constitution guarantees same-sex couples the right to marry. Obama had told an interviewer in 2014 that the Equal Protection Clause guarantees marriage in all fifty states, and the administration had filed against California’s Proposition 8. The White House is lit in rainbow colors the night of the ruling.

links.label: Social policy of the Obama administration

title: Iran nuclear deal is finalized in Vienna
tease: The JCPOA limits Iran’s nuclear program in exchange for sanctions relief, the payoff of Obama’s talk-without-preconditions line.
summary: On July 14, 2015, Iran and the P5+1 complete the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action. Iran accepts limits and inspections; the United States and partners ease nuclear-related sanctions. Formal talks began with a 2013 interim deal. The agreement is the foreign-policy counterpart of the 2007 Chicago speech’s willingness to negotiate with adversaries.

links.label: Foreign policy of the Obama administration

title: Rejects the Keystone XL border permit
tease: After years of review, Obama rejects the tar-sands pipeline as against the national interest and climate diplomacy.
summary: On November 6, 2015, Obama rejects TransCanada’s application to build the Keystone XL crossing from Alberta. He says the pipeline would not make a meaningful dent in U.S. gasoline prices and would undercut U.S. leadership heading into Paris. The project had sat in review since 2011, a de facto no that becomes an official no.

links.label: Energy policy of the Obama administration

title: Paris Agreement adopted
tease: Nearly 200 countries accept a climate pact. Obama uses executive tools after cap-and-trade dies in the Senate.
summary: The Paris Agreement is adopted December 12, 2015. Obama had wanted a domestic cap-and-trade bill in the first term; it dies after 2010. The second-term path is EPA’s Clean Power Plan, vehicle standards, and this diplomatic deal. He presents Paris as proof that U.S. credibility required killing Keystone XL a month earlier.

links.label: Energy policy of the Obama administration

title: Signs the Trans-Pacific Partnership
tease: The 12-nation trade pact is the economic arm of the Asia pivot. Congress never ratifies it.
summary: Trade ministers sign the Trans-Pacific Partnership in Auckland on February 4, 2016. Obama treats TPP as the economic half of a Pacific rebalance and a ruleset written without China. Both 2016 nominees campaign against it. The Senate never votes, and the United States later withdraws.

title: First sitting president in Cuba since Coolidge
tease: Obama lands in Havana, completing the 2014 thaw even as the statutory embargo remains on the books.
summary: On March 20, 2016, Obama arrives in Havana, the first sitting U.S. president to visit Cuba since Calvin Coolidge in 1928. Embassies had reopened in July 2015. The trip is the public end of a policy of isolation he spent most of his career leaving in place, with only family-travel easing before 2014.

title: U.S. abstains on UN settlement resolution 2334
tease: The outgoing administration withholds a veto as the Security Council condemns Israeli settlement activity.
summary: On December 23, 2016, the United States abstains on UN Security Council Resolution 2334, which says Israeli settlements have no legal validity. It is the sharpest public break of a presidency that otherwise kept military aid and a two-state frame, after years of fights with Benjamin Netanyahu over settlements and the Iran deal.

title: Leaves office with Guantanamo still open
tease: Forty-one men remain at the prison Obama ordered closed in 2009. Transfers cut the population; Congress blocked the rest.
summary: On Obama’s last full day in office, 41 detainees are still at Guantanamo. He never reverses the 2008–2009 position that the prison should close. Congress’s ban on transfers to the United States, plus politics around releasing remaining men, leaves the order unfulfilled. The stance and the outcome split.

links.label: Foreign policy of the Obama administration
